'''Tie:''' {{legend0|#DECDE6|40–50%}} {{legend0|#b3b3b3|No votes}} | title = [[Governor of Illinois|Governor]] | before_election = [[Pat Quinn (politician)|Pat Quinn]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = [[Bruce Rauner]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) | turnout = 48.48% {{decrease}} 1.21 [[percentage point|pp]] }} {{ElectionsIL}} The '''2014 Illinois gubernatorial election''' was held on November 4, 2014, to elect the [[Governor of Illinois|governor]] and [[Lieutenant Governor of Illinois|lieutenant governor of Illinois]], concurrently with the [[2014 United States Senate election in Illinois|election]] to Illinois's [[Classes of United States senators|Class II U.S. Senate seat]], as well as other elections to the [[2014 United States Senate elections|United States Senate]] in other states and elections to the [[2014 United States House of Representatives elections|United States House of Representatives]] and various state and local elections. Before this cycle, candidates for governor and lieutenant governor were nominated separately, and the primary winners ran on the same ticket in the general election. In 2011, the law was changed to allow candidates for governor to pick their own running mates. Incumbent Democratic Lieutenant Governor [[Sheila Simon]] did not run for reelection, instead running unsuccessfully [[2014 Illinois elections#Comptroller|for comptroller]]. She was replaced as Quinn's running mate by [[Paul Vallas]], a former [[Chief Executive Officer of Chicago Public Schools|CEO]] of [[Chicago Public Schools]]. Rauner chose [[Wheaton, Illinois|Wheaton]] City councilwoman [[Evelyn Sanguinetti]] as his running mate and Grimm chose Alex Cummings. Incumbent [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] governor [[Pat Quinn (politician)|Pat Quinn]] ran for re-election to a second full term in office. Quinn, then the lieutenant governor, assumed the office of governor on January 29, 2009, upon the [[Impeachment in the United States|impeachment]] and removal of [[Rod Blagojevich]]. He narrowly won a full term in [[2010 Illinois gubernatorial election|2010]]. Primary elections were held on March 18, 2014.{{cite web |url=http://www.elections.illinois.gov/ |title=Illinois State Board of Elections |publisher=Elections.illinois.gov |access-date=2015-01-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150331040020/http://www.elections.illinois.gov/ |archive-date=2015-03-31 |url-status=dead }} Quinn won the Democratic primary, while the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republicans]] chose businessman [[Bruce Rauner]] and the [[Libertarian Party (United States)|Libertarians]] nominated political activist Chad Grimm. Rauner defeated Quinn in the general election with 50.3% of the vote to Quinn's 46.4%, winning every county in the state except for [[Cook County]], home to the city of [[Chicago]] and 40% of the state's residents.{{cite web|url= https://www.huffingtonpost.com/2014/11/05/pat-quinn-concedes_n_6110092.html|title=Pat Quinn Concedes Illinois Gubernatorial Race to Bruce Rauner|work=[[Huffington Post]]|date=November 5, 2014|access-date=November 6, 2014}}Newman, James (November 5, 2014) - [http://www.niutoday.info/2014/11/05/think-quinnrauner-was-a-squeaker-and-durbinoberweis-was-a-cakewalk-heres-why-youd-be-wrong/ "Quinn/Rauner a Squeaker? Quinn was the only incumbent Democratic governor to lose a general election in 2014 and remained the last one to do so until [[Nevada]]'s [[Steve Sisolak]] in [[2022 Nevada gubernatorial election|2022]]. Rauner became the second Republican to be elected governor of Illinois while carrying all but one county, the other being [[Jim Edgar]] in [[1994 Illinois gubernatorial election|1994]]. This was the only time since 1998 that a Republican was elected Governor of Illinois. As of {{CURRENTYEAR}}, this alongside the concurrent comptroller election is the only time since 2010 that Republicans won a statewide election in Illinois. This is also the most recent Illinois gubernatorial election in which the winner won a majority of counties or won by a single-digit margin. Quinn later ran for Illinois Attorney General in [[2018 Illinois Attorney General election|2018]] and lost the Democratic primary. ==Background== The primaries and general elections coincided with those for federal ([[2014 United States House of Representatives elections in Illinois|House]] and [[2014 United States Senate election in Illinois|Senate]]) and those for other state offices.
